$comment: Landmarks, wonders, structures and sites — the places a person can stand in. A landmark is the one kind of element where being generically true is a failure: 'a castle in Croatia' is a category with a name stuck on it. What makes Nehaj Nehaj is that it was finished in 1558 by Ivan Lenkovic out of the stone of the churches and monasteries demolished outside Senj's walls, so a besieging Ottoman force could not shelter in them. That single fact explains its date, its material, its silhouette and its politics at once. This file exists to hold that depth, and to measure where the corpus has it and where it only has a name.
$rules: Every key is an element id. A place entry for an element that does not exist is an error, and so is a landmark element with no entry.
when / who / of / site are the four facts that make a place specific rather than generic. A place carrying none of them is a category wearing a proper noun.
of is what it is MADE of, and it should name elements this corpus already has, so a landmark joins the graph rather than hanging off it. For a natural wonder, of is the rock and the process.
site answers 'why here' — the fact about the ground that explains the building. A fortress on a bare hill in cannon range of its harbour is not the same claim as a fortress somewhere in Croatia.

wanted is the global checklist and it is the whole point of the file. Coverage measured against what we happen to have is not coverage; it is a total. Measured against a world list, a corpus of European castles reports itself as one.
Regions are the UN M49 subregions, unchanged, so the denominator is somebody else's and cannot be quietly redrawn to flatter the numerator.

A place whose element name differs from its checklist line names that line in `checklist`. The claim is explicit because a matcher loose enough to pair 'Kuk Swamp' with 'Kuk Early Agricultural Site' would also pair things that are not the same place, and a coverage number is only worth having if it never counts wrongly.

$src.note: Individual places carry their own srcTitle, resolved by tools/sources.mjs like every other citation in this repository.

kinds.name: Fortification
kinds.note: Walls, castles, forts. Built against somebody, which is why they carry the clearest politics of any structure.

kinds.name: Palace or seat
kinds.note: Where power sat, as distinct from where it defended itself.

kinds.name: Monument or statue
kinds.note: Built to be looked at rather than used.

kinds.name: Engineering work
kinds.note: Bridges, aqueducts, canals, roads, dams — the structures whose purpose is entirely function.

kinds.name: Settlement or site
kinds.note: Cities, archaeological sites, whole places rather than single buildings.

kinds.name: Industrial site
kinds.note: Mines, mills, furnaces, yards. The heritage that is usually listed last and demolished first.

kinds.name: Natural wonder
kinds.note: Not built. Derives from rock, water and time — and sometimes from living things, which is what makes Plitvice a different claim from a canyon.

kinds.name: Rock art or early mark
kinds.note: The oldest deliberate marks people left on places, and the only kind of site that is global at every date.

nehaj.who: Ivan Lenković, Croatian general and captain of the Uskoks
nehaj.site: a bare hill directly above Senj, in cannon range of the harbour, with nothing left standing around it to shelter a besieging force — the churches, monasteries and houses outside the walls were demolished and their stone went into the fortress
nehaj.size: 18 m tall, 23 m wide, walls 2-3 m thick, five towers, eleven cannon openings

senj.when: inhabited over 3,000 years; a Roman municipality from 35 BC
senj.who: Iapodes, then Rome, then the Habsburg frontier
senj.site: the seaward end of the Vratnik pass, where the only easy crossing of the Velebit reaches the Adriatic

plitvice.when: still forming — the barriers grow up to 13 mm a year; national park 1949, UNESCO 1979
plitvice.who: moss and algae, which is the whole point: the dams are built by living things
plitvice.site: a karst valley where groundwater arrives saturated with calcium hydrogencarbonate; sixteen lakes drop 133 m from the first to the last

velebit.when: Mesozoic limestone, uplifted with the Dinarides
velebit.site: 145 km from Senj to the source of the Zrmanja, the seaward wall of the Dinaric karst; highest point Vaganski vrh, 1,758 m

great_pyramid.site: the Giza plateau, a limestone shelf firm enough to carry six million tonnes, west of the Nile so the river could carry the casing stone to it

colosseum.who: begun under Vespasian, finished under Titus
colosseum.site: the drained lake of Nero’s Golden House, given back to the city as a public building on the site of a private palace

great_wall.when: walls from the 7th century BC; the brick-faced wall that survives is Ming, 14th to 17th century
great_wall.site: the line where farmland gives out and steppe begins, which is why the wall follows a rainfall boundary rather than a border

forbidden_city.site: the centre of Beijing on the north-south axis, walled and moated, with every hall facing south

terracotta_army.site: a pit complex about 1.5 km east of Qin Shi Huang's tomb mound, facing the direction his conquered enemies lay

angkor_wat.site: the Angkor plain, with five to ten million sandstone blocks brought about 40 km from Mount Kulen; a moat 190 m wide and over 5 km around, and — unusually for a Khmer temple — facing west

machu_picchu.site: a ridge between two peaks above the Urubamba

ishtar_gate.site: the eighth gate of Babylon's inner wall, opening onto the processional way, so it was the first thing a visitor saw

lighthouse_of_alexandria.when: built about 280-247 BC; brought down by earthquakes between 956 and 1323
lighthouse_of_alexandria.site: the island of Pharos at the harbour mouth, on a coast so flat that a ship had no landmark to steer by without it

mausoleum_halicarnassus.site: a hillside above the harbour of Halicarnassus, visible from the sea it was meant to be admired from

colossus_of_rhodes.when: built 292-280 BC; fell in an earthquake about 226 BC, after 54 years
colossus_of_rhodes.site: the harbour of Rhodes, paid for by selling the siege equipment an unsuccessful besieger left behind

temple_of_artemis.when: the marble temple about 550 BC, burned 356 BC, rebuilt, destroyed 262 AD
temple_of_artemis.site: a marshy site near Ephesus chosen deliberately — soft ground was thought to cushion earthquakes

statue_of_zeus.site: inside the temple at Olympia, built so large for the space that Zeus would have taken the roof off if he stood up

hanging_gardens.who: attributed to Nebuchadnezzar II — and never securely located
hanging_gardens.when: described in Greek sources from the 3rd century BC onward
hanging_gardens.site: never securely located — no Babylonian text mentions them, and one reading puts them at Nineveh instead

lanse_aux_meadows.site: a landing at the northern tip of Newfoundland
lanse_aux_meadows.when: about 1021 AD, dated by a solar storm recorded in the wood

nabta_playa.site: a seasonal lakebed in the Nubian Desert
nabta_playa.when: occupied from about 9000 BCE; the stone circle around 4800 BCE
nabta_playa.who: cattle-herding people of the Nubian Desert

lalibela.when: late 12th to early 13th century, under Gebre Meskel Lalibela of the Zagwe
lalibela.site: a highland plateau of scoriaceous basalt soft enough to cut and sound enough to stand once the trenches are open

great_zimbabwe.when: built from the 11th century, the Great Enclosure 13th-15th, abandoned in the 16th or 17th
great_zimbabwe.site: granite hills that exfoliate in flat sheets under daily heating and cooling, so the building stone arrives already the right shape and needs no mortar

olduvai_gorge.when: beds spanning 1.85 million to 600,000 years ago; Zinjanthropus found July 1959, Homo habilis May 1960
olduvai_gorge.who: Homo habilis and Homo erectus, then Louis and Mary Leakey
olduvai_gorge.site: 48 km of gorge eroded up to 90 m into Pleistocene lake beds, so the sequence stands exposed in order

aksum_obelisk.when: 4th century CE; removed to Rome 1937, returned 2005, re-erected 2008
aksum_obelisk.site: the stelae field at Aksum, on the trade road between the Red Sea and the highlands

kilwa_kisiwani.when: Great Mosque begun 1131-1170; the city's peak 13th to 15th centuries
kilwa_kisiwani.who: Swahili merchants; Husuni Kubwa built for Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman
kilwa_kisiwani.site: an island with no building stone and a harbour commanding the route to the Sofala gold

mapungubwe.site: the confluence of the Limpopo and the Shashe, on the inland end of the Indian Ocean gold route

twyfelfontein.when: engravings roughly 6,000 to 1,000 years old; UNESCO 2007
twyfelfontein.site: sandstone slabs around a spring in the Damaraland desert — the Damara name means jumping waterhole

ngorongoro.when: the volcano active 2.45 to 2 million years ago, then collapsed
ngorongoro.site: a caldera 610 m deep with a 260 km2 floor, whose rim holds grazing and water together so about 25,000 large animals stay put

uluru.when: the Mutitjulu Arkose laid down 550-530 million years ago
uluru.site: a bed of coarse arkose tipped almost vertical and left standing when the softer rock around it eroded away; 348 m above the plain, 9.4 km around, most of it still underground

budj_bim.when: one trap carbon-dated to 6,600 years; the wider system estimated up to 8,000
budj_bim.site: the Tyrendarra lava flow, which blocked the old drainage and made the wetlands the system steers

sydney_opera_house.site: Bennelong Point, a peninsula seen from three sides, which is why the roof had to work as a fifth elevation

great_barrier_reef.when: the present reef about 500,000 years old, the living veneer around 8,000
great_barrier_reef.who: coral polyps — the largest structure any living thing has built
great_barrier_reef.site: a shallow continental shelf in warm clear water, which is the only place reef-building coral can work

moai.site: Rano Raraku, one quarry of compressed volcanic ash that supplied all but 53 of more than 900 figures; 394 are still there unfinished

nan_madol.when: settled around AD 1; megalithic building from about 1180
nan_madol.site: a coral reef flat off Temwen Island, cut by tidal canals into 92 artificial islets over 1.5 by 0.5 km

skara_brae.when: occupied about 3180 to 2500 BC; uncovered by a storm in 1850
skara_brae.site: a treeless island where the only building material is flagstone, so even the beds and dressers are stone; buried in a dune until a storm took it off

newgrange.when: about 3100 BC; the solstice alignment first re-observed 21 December 1967
newgrange.who: Neolithic builders of the Boyne valley
newgrange.site: a ridge above the Boyne, oriented so the roof-box admits the midwinter sunrise down a 19 m passage; the mound is 85 m across and 12 m high

lascaux.when: 17,000 to 22,000 years old; found 12 September 1940, closed to the public 1963
lascaux.site: a sealed limestone cave in the Dordogne whose stable air preserved the pigment — and whose stability is exactly what visitors destroyed

iron_bridge.who: designed by Thomas Farnolls Pritchard, cast by Abraham Darby III
iron_bridge.site: the Severn gorge at Coalbrookdale, where the river had to be crossed and the foundry that could cast the ribs was already on the bank

wieliczka.when: documented from 1044, shaft-mined from the 13th century, sold salt until 1996
wieliczka.who: generations of miners, who carved the chapels themselves
wieliczka.site: a salt bed near Krakow, 327 m deep with 287 km of galleries

gobekli_tepe.site: a limestone ridge above the Harran plain; four enclosures excavated of about twenty, 10 to 30 m across

petra.when: Nabataean capital from the 2nd century BC, at its height in the 1st century AD with about 20,000 people
petra.site: a sandstone basin entered through the Siq, a natural cleft 3-4 m wide, watered entirely by dams, conduits and cisterns the Nabataeans built

borobudur.when: begun about 780 CE, finished about 833, under the Sailendra
borobudur.site: a hill on the Kedu Plain between volcanoes, with the Progo riverbed supplying 55,000 cubic metres of andesite; 118 m to a side, 35 m high

nazca_lines.who: the Paracas and then the Nazca
nazca_lines.site: a rainless windless plateau whose limey subsoil hardens into a crust — the only reason 1,300 km of shallow line has lasted two thousand years

djenne_mosque.when: the present building completed 1907; the first mosque here 13th-14th century
djenne_mosque.who: the masons' guild of Djenné, and the whole town every year
djenne_mosque.site: a platform 3 m above the marketplace, which is what keeps the Bani flood out of a building made of earth

citadelle_laferriere.who: Henri Christophe — at a cost of up to 20,000 lives
citadelle_laferriere.site: the 900 m summit of Bonnet à l'Évêque, several kilometres inland, so any French landing would have to climb to it; 365 cannon and stores for 5,000 men for a year

registan.site: the square at the centre of Samarkand, where proclamations were read and executions held, on the Silk Road

kuk_swamp.when: drainage from about 9,000 years ago; bananas and sugar cane by 6,900 to 6,400
kuk_swamp.site: a highland wetland at the edge of taro's range, drained by three grades of ditch; 116 hectares protected, UNESCO 2008

mohenjo_daro.when: built about 2500 BCE, abandoned about 1700 BCE; rediscovered in the 1920s
mohenjo_daro.site: the Indus floodplain — over 700 wells, one per three houses, and drains along a rectilinear grid

cahokia.when: population rose from under 3,000 to over 10,000 between 1050 and 1100; abandoned by 1400
cahokia.site: the Mississippi floodplain where maize would grow; about 120 earthworks, Monks Mound 30 m high and 622,000 cubic metres

teotihuacan.when: founded about 100 BCE, peak 350-650 CE, palaces burned about 550 CE
teotihuacan.who: unknown — the founders' origin and language are both undetermined
teotihuacan.site: a valley with obsidian nearby; an avenue 2 km long and 45 m wide, and a pyramid of over a million cubic metres

chartres.when: rebuilt 1194-1220 after a fire, re-consecrated October 1260
chartres.who: unknown masons — no architect is named
chartres.site: a hill above the Eure, on a crypt and towers that survived the fire and were built into the new church

mont_saint_michel.when: the first church from 708; the abbey built up from the 8th century onward
mont_saint_michel.who: Benedictine monks, after Aubert of Avranches
mont_saint_michel.site: a leucogranite outcrop 92 m high and 960 m around, in a bay with a 14 m tidal range — an island twice a day, and free defence the rest of the time

mbanza_kongo.when: founded about 1390, capital until the kingdom was abolished in 1915; UNESCO 2017
mbanza_kongo.who: Lukeni lua Nimi, then the kings of Kongo
mbanza_kongo.site: a mountain top at a junction of major trade routes; about 130,000 people in the city and its hinterland by the 1620s

diocletians_palace.when: begun about 295, finished by 305 when Diocletian abdicated
diocletians_palace.site: the Adriatic coast near the Brač quarries that supplied it; when Salona fell in the 7th century its refugees moved inside the walls, and about 3,000 people still live there

dubrovnik_walls.when: mainly 13th-17th centuries, the peak from the early 15th to the late 16th
dubrovnik_walls.site: a rock promontory with the sea on three sides, so the landward wall runs 4 to 6 m thick and the seaward as little as 1.5; 1,940 m around, up to 25 m high

pula_arena.when: 27 BC to AD 68, expanded under Vespasian and finished under Titus in 81
pula_arena.site: a slope outside the town walls, which carries part of the seating; 132.5 by 105.1 m, about 23,000 seats, and the only Roman amphitheatre with its whole outer ring still standing

horyuji.when: the pagoda's central pillar felled in 594; Japan's first UNESCO site, 1993
horyuji.site: the Nara basin; over 180 national treasures on one temple site, and the oldest standing wooden buildings in the world

giants_causeway.when: the lava erupted 50 to 60 million years ago, in the Paleocene
giants_causeway.site: a coast cut back by the sea through the inside of a lava flow — about 40,000 columns, mostly hexagonal, the tallest around 12 m

stonehenge.when: built in stages from about 3000 BC, the sarsen circle about 2500 BC
stonehenge.who: Neolithic and Early Bronze Age builders
stonehenge.site: Salisbury Plain, with sarsens hauled about 25 km from the Marlborough Downs and bluestones some 250 km from the Preseli hills

hadrians_wall.when: begun AD 122, most of it built in about six years
hadrians_wall.who: Legio II Augusta, VI Victrix and XX Valeria Victrix — about 15,000 men
hadrians_wall.site: the narrowest part of Britain, 117 km coast to coast; a ditch in front, the Vallum behind, a milecastle every Roman mile and a turret every third

mesa_verde.when: cliff dwellings mainly 1150-1300; abandoned about 1285 after the drought of 1276-1299
mesa_verde.site: alcoves undercut where seeping water meets a shale band inside the Cliff House Sandstone — dry, shaded in summer, sunlit in winter, and out of the rain

malbork.when: built over 132 years, 1274-1406; over half destroyed in 1945, restored since 1962
malbork.site: the Nogat river on a plain with no building stone, so the order fired its own — 21 hectares inside the outer walls

chichen_itza.when: the city from about 600 CE; El Castillo in its present form 11th-13th century
chichen_itza.who: the Maya of the northern Yucatán
chichen_itza.site: four cenotes in one place, on a peninsula whose limestone drains every river underground — the water is the reason the city is here

sigiriya.site: a granite inselberg 180 m above the plain, with one stair up through a gateway built as a lion, and water gardens at the foot that run on gravity

hagia_sophia.when: built 532-537; the dome rebuilt after collapse in 558. Church to 1453, mosque to 1935, museum to 2020, mosque since
hagia_sophia.who: Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus
hagia_sophia.site: the first hill of Constantinople above the Bosphorus, on an active fault — which is why the first dome came down and the second was built steeper

sacsayhuaman.when: built in the 15th century under the Inca
sacsayhuaman.who: Inca masons — Cieza de León reports 20,000 men
sacsayhuaman.site: the ridge above Cusco, with the stone hauled about 35 km from Rumicolca; three terrace walls, the longest about 400 m and 6 m high

eiffel_tower.when: built 28 January 1887 to 31 March 1889, opened 15 May 1889
eiffel_tower.site: the Champ de Mars for the 1889 exposition; 330 m tall on a 125 m square base, and it moves 9 cm in wind and 18 cm away from the sun

himeji.when: a fort from 1333, the present castle 1601-1609; restored 2010-2015
himeji.site: a hill over the road west from the capital; 83 buildings, and a path to the keep 325 m long where the straight line is 130

pont_du_gard.when: about 40-60 AD, roughly fifteen years to build
pont_du_gard.site: the narrowest crossing of the Gardon on a 50 km line that had to fall one metre in three thousand the whole way

potala.when: begun 1645; the shell in three years, the interior in forty-five
potala.site: Marpo Ri hill at about 3,700 m on a seismic fault — 400 m east to west, 119 m high, walls battered inward and tied with copper in the foundations

benin_moat.when: the Inner City Iya about 1460; moat building possibly from as early as 800
benin_moat.who: the Edo of the Kingdom of Benin
benin_moat.site: around Benin City — the inner moat about 12 km, and up to 17 m from ditch floor to rampart top. Estimates of 16,000 km for the wider Edo earthworks are a sum of many separate structures of different dates, not one wall

merv.when: Achaemenid through Timurid; possibly the world's largest city by 1150; sacked by the Mongols in 1221
merv.who: four dynasties, each building beside the last rather than over it
merv.site: an oasis on the road across the Karakum where caravans had to stop; Sultan Sanjar's mausoleum is 27 m to a side and its turquoise dome was said to be visible a day's march away

ha_long_bay.when: karst developing since the Miocene, about 20 million years
ha_long_bay.site: a drowned tower-karst landscape: some 1,600 islands of Carboniferous and Permian limestone, most towers 50 to 100 m high and about six times taller than wide, each notched by the sea at the same level

tikal.when: monumental building from the 4th century BC, at its height about 200-900, abandoned by the end of the 10th century
tikal.site: a plateau in the Petén with no river, lake or cenote — the city ran on rain caught off plastered plazas and held in reservoirs

bagan.when: 11th to 13th centuries; the 1975 earthquake damaged many and 2016 damaged nearly 400 more
bagan.who: the Pagan Empire — merit-making by whoever could afford a temple
bagan.site: a dry plain in the bend of the Irrawaddy, where more than 10,000 temples went up in two centuries and about 2,200 survive

caral.when: about 2600 to 2000 BC — 1,500 years before the Olmec
caral.who: the Norte Chico, about 3,000 people here
caral.site: the Supe valley, one of nineteen related sites; the main pyramid 150 by 110 m and 28 m high, with no battlements, no weapons and no pottery anywhere

krak_des_chevaliers.when: built out by the Hospitallers 1142-1170 and again in the 13th century; surrendered 8 April 1271
krak_des_chevaliers.site: the Homs Gap, the one easy route from the Syrian interior to the coast — which is why a garrison of 2,000 sat there

taj_mahal.site: a bend of the Yamuna at Agra, laid out on a north-south axis in bilateral symmetry, with the minarets leaning outward so a fall would take them away from the tomb

chaco_canyon.when: the major period 900 to 1150; most construction beams cut 1033-1092
chaco_canyon.site: a dry canyon with no timber at all, fed by six road systems up to 97 km long and 9 m wide, dead straight regardless of terrain, in a culture with no wheel and no draught animal

brooklyn_bridge.who: John A. Roebling, then Washington Roebling, then Emily Warren Roebling
brooklyn_bridge.site: the East River, too deep and too busy for piers in the channel; 486 m of main span, and 110 cases of decompression sickness in the caissons in four months of 1872

kizhi_pogost.when: the Transfiguration Church's altar laid 6 June 1714; the Intercession rebuilt 1764; dismantled and reassembled 1999-2014
kizhi_pogost.site: an island in Lake Onega, built from Scots pine logs about 30 cm thick and 3 to 5 m long — the restoration numbered and photographed every beam before taking it apart

caribbean: Taino rock art of Cueva de las Maravillas — rock_art
south_europe: Statue of Zeus at Olympia — monument
